target_customer: Banks and financial institutions in Latin America that originate loans (at YC time the company was Philippo, serving home sellers and buyers)
problem: Banks in Latin America run slow, manual loan origination; the founders first tried to solve liquidity for home sellers with Philippo.
business_model: B2B SaaS loan origination platform (earlier: property-backed advance financed by capital)
product_category: Fintech, loan origination software (earlier proptech lending)

founders.name: Guido Galanter
founders.background_notes: YC page: led New Ventures at OLX and worked on Naspers M&A including the Frontier Car Group deal.

founders.name: Tomas Gropper
prior_employers: Largest retailer in Argentina (unnamed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Head of Engineering at the retailer per the YC page.

founders.name: Nicolas Piqueras
education: Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, Economics and Finance
founders.background_notes: Led corporate finance and capital markets, coordinated two NYSE IPOs per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Loan origination software needs integrations with bank core systems and credit bureaus in several countries, a moderately hard enterprise engineering task for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated into a bank workflow it is sticky, but at founding the capital-heavy Philippo model had no technical moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the business.

market_need_then: Digital lending in Argentina was growing quickly in 2021 and 2022 (Naranja X, Uala and banks reported rising digital loan volumes per Iupana and other 2022 coverage), and banks were pressed to speed up credit decisions.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B tone, loan lifecycle efficiency

rebrands.why: Reported by a search summary as a pivot after rising rates hurt the capital-intensive model; not confirmed in a source opened, so treat as unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; a B2B name used since a pivot.

pivots.from: Philippo: property sale advance of up to 75 percent of appraised value, based in Chile
pivots.to: Lenk: loan origination software for LATAM banks
pivots.why: Search summary attributes it to rising interest rates against a capital-intensive model; unverified

outcome_analysis: Lenk is listed as active. It began as Philippo, a capital-heavy home liquidity lender, and moved to selling loan origination software to banks, a lighter model that fits the founders' corporate finance and engineering backgrounds. No verified funding or traction figures exist, so the outcome beyond survival is unknown.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators disagree (CB Insights about $520K total including Y Combinator, Magma Partners, Start-Up Chile and Soma Capital; VCBacked $2.0M; Startupintros $600K seed; PitchBook $20M). A Diario Financiero headline cites US$20M from Frontal Trust for Philippo, terms unknown, probably a credit facility. None recorded as rounds. Competitor list left empty: no dated source for rivals to the Philippo home-advance model was found; Digiventures, a loan origination startup in the same W22 batch, is a peer for the later Lenk model but no dated source was opened. Lenk website blocked with 403 and was not worked around.
